papers.title: Forest management, climate change, and roe deer: A conceptual model of how silvicultural systems shape habitat, population density, and browsing impacts
papers.authors: Sebastian Schwegmann, Max Kröschel, João Manuel Cordeiro Pereira, Andreea Petronela Spînu, Andreas Rigling
papers.source: OpenAlex / Forest Ecology and Management
papers.abstract: Management of roe deer in European forests may be challenging due to their impact on tree regeneration and potential negative effects on tree species composition, forest resilience and various ecosystem services including timber production. However, silvicultural practices themselves are key drivers in shaping roe deer habitat and consequently affecting deer population densities and the browsing susceptibility of young trees. Silvicultural interventions shape forest structures such as canopy closure, and thus the light availability and thermal cover at the forest floor. Light availability on the forest floor in turn determines vegetation growth and therefore forage availability and quality, as well as hiding opportunities for roe deer. Additionally, natural disturbances such as bark beetle outbreaks increasingly affect European forests at different spatial scales, influencing the interactions between roe deer and forests, while also underscoring the need for increased forest resilience amid climate change. papers.title: Global climatic suitability and future distribution of Hypsipyla grandella : Implications for Meliaceae under climate change
papers.authors: Daiane das Graças do Carmo, Letícia Caroline da Silva Sant'Ana, Damaris Rosa de Freitas, Alice Barbutti Barreto Maranhão, Bianca Sabina Olmedo Monteiro Ferreira
papers.source: OpenAlex / Agricultural and Forest Entomology
papers.abstract: Abstract Hypsipyla grandella Zeller (Lepidoptera: Pyralidae) is one of the main pests of species in the Meliaceae family, and predicting areas of climatic suitability for this species is important for planning pest management strategies and implementing phytosanitary policies. This study aimed to determine the areas of climatic suitability for H. grandella worldwide, under current conditions and future climate change scenarios A maximum entropy (MaxEnt) model was used to estimate the global climatic suitability of H. grandella based on occurrence records and climatic variables related to temperature and precipitation. Climatic variables related to temperature and precipitation were the most influential factors in determining the species' environmental suitability. The model showed a high correspondence between occurrence records and areas classified as highly suitable, concentrated mainly in Central America, the Caribbean and tropical South America. papers.title: Development of research on retention forestry over the last four decades
papers.authors: Lena Gustafsson
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Forest Research
papers.abstract: Four decades ago, a modified form of forest management was introduced with the aim of reconciling wood production and environmental values. Central is the deliberate retention at harvest of structural components key to biodiversity and ecological processes such as old trees, dead trees and specific tree species. This “retention forestry” model was initially implemented in clearcutting forestry but has later been introduced also in continuous-cover forestry and is today widespread on different continents. This review describes and analyses scientific publications on retention forestry in boreal and temperate regions with a focus on biodiversity, a key aspect of the model, based on a systematic literature search. The expansion of the practical application of the model in different parts of the world is described, as well as large-scale experiments. The use of terms associated with retention forestry (green-tree retention”, “variable retention”, “microhabitat”, “lifeboating”, “biological legacy”) regionally and over time is described. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. papers.authors: Ricardo B. Vigan
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Sustainable and Integrated Studies
papers.abstract: This study assessed the knowledge and practices of Grade 12 Organic Agriculture students of Gamu Agri-Fishery School in Linglingay, Gamu, Isabela, and examined the relationship between these two variables. Anchored on a Knowledge–Practice Framework informed by experiential and competency-based learning, the study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional descriptive-correlational design. Total enumeration was used involving all 35 Grade 12 Organic Agriculture students. Data were gathered through a researcher-developed structured questionnaire consisting of an objective knowledge assessment and a frequency-based practice scale. Descriptive statistics and Spearman’s rank-order correlation were employed in analyzing the data. Results showed a high level of knowledge, with an overall performance of 85.43% and 88.57% of the respondents classified as having high or very high knowledge. Organic agriculture practices were also consistently demonstrated, with an overall mean of 3.57 and 94.29% of respondents classified under the “Always” category. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.title: Comparing literature-guided, LLM-assisted, and data-driven models for predicting angler pressure
papers.authors: Azar Taheri Tayebi, Julia S. Schmid, Sean Simmons, Mark S. Poesch, Mark A. Lewis
papers.source: OpenAlex / PLoS ONE
papers.abstract: This study compared three models-a literature-guided, a large language model (LLM)-assisted, and a data-driven model-all developed using Bayesian networks as the framework for predicting angler pressure measured by the number of boats observed in aerial surveys. The models used meteorological data from 98 lakes in Ontario, Canada, during 2018 and 2019, as well as platform-derived variables, including angler-reported fishing trips, fishing duration, and catch rate, together with lake webpage views. In five-fold cross-validation, no pairwise difference in fold-level accuracy among the three models remained significant after Holm adjustment. These findings suggest that LLM-assisted model construction has potential to support ecological prediction when paired with empirical validation.

papers.abstract: Landscape architecture in Thailand still relies heavily on commercially propagated species. While convenient,this dependence narrows the design palette and promotes inclusion of exotic species or ecologically unsuitableplants, undermining biodiversity, long-term sustainability, and ecological resilience. By contrast, sustainablelandscape architecture prioritizes indigenous and locally adapted species that are visually expressive yetecologically matched to local conditions, thereby reducing maintenance, supporting native biota, and articulatingregional identity. This research was done to investigate the effect of drought stress, soil salinity, Piriformospora indica (P. indica), and MWCNs on biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil that contaminated with Pb and Cd under cultivation of triticale plant. After 70 days, plants were harvested, and plant and soil Cd were measured using AAS (atomic absorption spectrometry). In addition, the degradation percentage of diesel oil in soil was determined. papers.title: Methyl jasmonate (MeJA) as an elicitor enhances tomato resistance through ROS and digestive enzyme inhibition against Helicoverpa armigera (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae)
papers.authors: Raheleh Jahanbin-Navrod, Reza Shirzadian-Khorramabad, Arash Zibaee, Zahra Hajiahmadi
papers.source: OpenAlex / Scientific Reports
papers.abstract: Methyl jasmonate (MeJA) is a central regulator of plant defense, yet the physiological consequences of MeJA-induced defenses for herbivorous insects remain incompletely resolved across multiple levels of herbivore performance. Here, we investigated how exogenous MeJA treatment of tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum ) modulates plant oxidative defenses and the subsequent digestive, antioxidant, and nutritional physiology of Helicoverpa armigera larvae. MeJA elicitation induced a significant, dose-dependent H₂O₂-associated response in tomato leaves, with DAB-derived staining extending across approximately 98% of the leaf area at 1 mM MeJA, accompanied by a 45% increase in peroxidase (POD) activity. Feeding third-instar larvae on MeJA-elicited foliage increased mortality from 13% in controls to > 60% at 1 mM MeJA and reduced larval length by up to 68%. These effects coincided with pronounced alterations in midgut digestive physiology, with trypsin, chymotrypsin, α-amylase, and lipase activities decreasing by approximately 45–65%. Larval antioxidant responses were likewise markedly altered, with catalase (CAT) activity declining by approximately 99.7% and POD activity by approximately 42–47.

High- and low-resistance materials screened from each perspective were further analyzed by widely targeted LC-MS metabolomics. The three damage indices differed highly significantly among clones (P<0.01) and were positively correlated, indicating abundant genetic variation in resistance. Clones such as Ⅲ-30-C, Ⅱ-35-A and Ⅰ-21-A showed strong overall resistance, whereas Ⅱ-28-E and Ⅳ-20-A showed high constitutive and induced resistance.
